scope: Two-browser-tab concurrent refresh: does revokeFamily() revoke Tab A's newly inserted token? Ordering analysis.

evidence.observation: revokeFamily() runs two synchronous UPDATEs in sequence. Statement 1 marks the family row revoked. Statement 2 marks all matching refresh_tokens with revoked_at IS NULL as revoked.
The WHERE clause is 'family_id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL'. This UPDATE only affects tokens that ALREADY EXIST at the moment it runs. A token inserted after this UPDATE is not affected.
insert() creates the new row with revoked_at implicitly NULL. It does NOT check whether the family is already revoked before inserting.
isFamilyRevoked() reads ONLY from token_families. After Tab B's revokeFamily() sets token_families.revoked_at, isFamilyRevoked() returns true for this family forever.

evidence.quote:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens (
   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
   family_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES token_families(id),
   user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
   token_hash TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
   created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
   expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
   revoked_at INTEGER NULL
 );
evidence.observation: No CHECK constraint prevents inserting a new token into a revoked family. The foreign key only guarantees the family row exists, not that it is unrevoked.

hypotheses.statement: Because Tab B's revokeFamily() is synchronous and runs to completion before Tab A resumes, Tab B's UPDATE always executes before Tab A's INSERT. Therefore Tab A's new token is NEVER caught by revokeFamily()'s UPDATE — it escapes into the DB with revoked_at=NULL in a revoked family.

Tab A's new token row is inserted with revoked_at=NULL into a family whose token_families.revoked_at is set. isFamilyRevoked() will return true for this family. Any future use of this token (for /me, /orders, /cart, or another refresh) will be rejected by isFamilyRevoked() check in authMiddleware.

The schema has no constraint to prevent this insertion. The only way to prevent Tab A from inserting into a revoked family is to check isFamilyRevoked() inside rotate() before insert(), or to wrap the entire read-check-revoke-insert sequence in a database transaction.
